text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called the “silent killer” because it usually has no warning signs or symptoms. You can have high blood pressure for years without feeling anything while it quietly damages your heart, blood vessels, and kidneys.
snippet_highlighted_words: it usually has no warning signs or symptoms

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms rarely happen unless your blood pressure is dangerously high or reaches a hypertensive crisis (above 180/120 mm Hg). When symptoms do occur, they may include:
If your blood pressure is higher than 180/120 mm Hg and you experience any of the following warning signs, seek emergency medical help right away:

list.snippet: Chest pain or radiating pain to the arm, neck, or jaw
Trouble walking, balance issues, or signs of a stroke

text_blocks.snippet: Because symptoms are not a reliable way to detect high blood pressure, regular monitoring is the only safe approach. You can check your numbers during routine doctor visits or at home using a cuff monitor.
Guidance on tracking and managing your readings is available through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
